hypothesis: Implied volatility quoted on SPY and QQQ exceeds the realised volatility subsequently observed over the following 5 trading days, by a positive average amount, on this account's own IBKR data. This is a statement about a statistical gap, NOT about tradeable return.
gate: PASS iff, for BOTH SPY and QQQ scored separately and never pooled: at least 60 non-overlapping 5-day windows are available; the mean VARIANCE premium (IV_t^2 - RV^2_[t,t+5]) is positive; and its 95% confidence interval, from resampling whole non-overlapping windows, excludes zero. Any IV value outside [0.01, 3.0] annualised aborts the run as a unit mismatch rather than being scored. A PASS establishes only that the premium exists in this data; it authorises stage 2 (a defined-risk structure priced with real options and costs) and nothing else. No position is implied and no return is claimed.

timeSplit.note: Whole available IV history, ~502 daily observations per underlying. No train/holdout split: this stage estimates a descriptive quantity rather than fitting anything, so there is no parameter to overfit and nothing to hold out from.

symbolSplit.note: SPY and QQQ scored independently and both required to clear. They correlate ~0.9 and are never pooled into a single n.

costAssumptions.note: None applied at stage 1, because no position is taken. Cost modelling is stage 2's entire difficulty and the premium must be large enough to survive it there.

notes: Premium is measured on VARIANCE, not volatility: the sample standard deviation is a biased estimator of sigma at small n (c4 ~ 0.95 at h=5), worth about -1.08 vol points on a 0.18 series, which is the same sign and roughly the size of the effect being hunted. Measuring IV - RV directly would have produced a confident premium from a series containing none. Horizon fixed at 5 trading days on power grounds before any data was seen: h=21 yields only 22 independent windows and a ~2.4-3.6 vol-point minimum detectable effect, above the documented size of the premium.

hypothesis: Before building an FX carry study, determine whether the available data could detect a carry premium of the size the literature documents (2-5%/yr). This is a question about the STUDY, not about markets.
gate: PROCEED iff the effective sample can detect a 3%/yr premium at 80% power and alpha 0.05. Otherwise the study is not built, because a null from an underpowered test is uninterpretable and would go on the record as though it were evidence.

resultSummary.question: Can 5 years of monthly FX data detect a documented 2-5%/yr carry premium?

sd2.0%.summary: UNDERPOWERED: needs 503 independent observations, has 61 (8.2x short). Smallest detectable effect is 0.0072 /mo, but the effect sought is 0.0025 /mo. A null from this study would mean nothing.

sd2.5%.summary: UNDERPOWERED: needs 786 independent observations, has 61 (12.9x short). Smallest detectable effect is 0.0090 /mo, but the effect sought is 0.0025 /mo. A null from this study would mean nothing.

hypothesis: The trend-gated breakout entry adds value by DECLINING to be long weak names, not by timing strong ones. On the 30-symbol survivorship-biased bundle its excess over a matched-geometry random entry is +0.0064R overall (p=0.4741), -0.0851R on the ten best buy-and-hold performers, and +0.3646R on the ten worst (p=0.0767). That split is POST-HOC -- the subgroups were defined by an outcome only knowable at the end -- and the laggard excess sits below the 0.696R this test could detect, so it is a diagnostic and not a finding. It predicts that a universe containing genuine failures rather than 30 survivors would show a LARGER excess than +0.0064R, because the cases the gate exists to avoid are the ones this bundle removed.
gate: On a survivorship-free universe chosen by a rule fixed in advance (e.g. every S&P 500 constituent as of 2023-01-01, delisted names included, held in the index at that date and not re-selected later), the same unchanged configuration must show an excess over a matched-geometry random entry that is BOTH positive and at or above the minimum detectable effect at 80% power for that sample. Anything less -- including a positive excess that the test could not have detected -- FAILS. A larger absolute balance is not evidence and does not count.

runFile: sp500-bundle/1440 (128 symbols after dropping SBNY as a reused ticker), 2023-01-03..2026-09-02, cost model usEquityRetail
resultSummary: REFUTED, with the sign reversed. The gate required an excess over a matched-geometry random entry that was positive AND at or above the minimum detectable effect. On 128 symbols and 1,181 trades the overall excess is +0.0183R (p=0.3932, MDE 0.218) -- not detectable. On the subgroup the hypothesis was about, the 38 symbols that LOST money buy-and-hold, the excess is -0.1175R (p=0.8225): the strategy is WORSE than random on falling names, not better. It worsens monotonically with weakness -- worst 20 -0.2752R, worst 10 -0.3650R. The +0.3646R laggard excess seen on the 30-symbol bundle was noise and reversed sign on a sample four times larger, which is what an underpowered post-hoc subgroup does. CAVEAT ON THE UNIVERSE, which does not rescue the result: Yahoo serves almost no delisted history, so the genuine failures are absent -- of ten delisted names attempted (SIVB, FRC, PACW, DISH, CTLT, PXD, MRO, WBA, CMA, IPG) exactly zero usable series were obtained, and the SBNY that did arrive is a reused ticker starting 2024-08-15, not the bank that failed in 2023. The universe still contains 38 names that lost money including CHPT -97%, LCID -92%, SEDG -88%, ENPH -86%, so the hypothesis had ample population to show itself in and did not; it showed the opposite.

hypothesis: The dollar-neutral cross-sectional momentum spread -- rank by 252-bar return skipping the last 21, hold the top decile long and the bottom decile short, rebalance every 21 bars -- carries a real risk-adjusted edge that will persist forward. In-sample over 31 monthly periods it returned 29.44% CAGR at a 10.09% drawdown net of 5% annualised borrow, beat a random-split-of-the-same-names null at p=0.0050, and held out of sample at 35.14% CAGR over 20 quarterly-refit periods. It FAILED two gate conditions: raw return below SPY (0.02150 monthly against 0.02251), and 31 effective periods against 32 required.
gate: Over at least 32 forward monthly periods beginning 2026-09-03, using the FROZEN configuration and the FROZEN universe recorded here, with costs at 5bp per leg per rebalance and 5% annualised borrow on the short half, ALL of the following must hold: (1) mean monthly log return strictly above zero; (2) the spread beats a random-split null of the same names at p < 0.05; (3) maximum drawdown at or below 25%. Any one failing is a FAIL. A larger balance is not evidence and does not substitute for any of the three. MOMENTUM-CRASH CLAUSE: if the forward window contains a market decline of 20% or more followed by a recovery, that sub-period is reported SEPARATELY and in full whatever it shows, because a post-bottom rebound is this strategy family's documented failure mode and is entirely absent from the sample the hypothesis was formed on. A result that omits it is incomplete regardless of the headline.

symbolSplit.holdout: the same 128, frozen; no re-selection is permitted

costAssumptions.source: costs.mjs plus a flat borrow charge on the short half
